title: Classical and Folk Dances of India: Quiz

questions.question: How many classical dance forms of India are recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
questions.rationale: Eight — with Sattriya of Assam the most recent (recognised in 2000), joining the seven classics of the older lists.

questions.question: The classical dance form associated with the sattra monasteries of Assam is:
questions.rationale: Sankardev created Sattriya within the Vaishnavite sattra institutions — the monastery link is the clue that names the form.

questions.question: Which classical dance is traditionally performed without ankle bells (ghungroos)?
questions.rationale: Manipuri's soft, rounded aesthetic treats percussion as external (the pung drum), not worn on the ankles — a one-fact question that recurs annually.

questions.question: The 'tarangam' — dancing on the rim of a brass plate — belongs to:
questions.rationale: Kuchipudi's signature plate balance comes from the Bhagavata Mela tradition codified by Siddhendra Yogi in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: The Natyashastra, the founding treatise of Indian dramaturgy and dance, is attributed to:
questions.rationale: Bharata Muni's Natyashastra (c. 200 BCE-200 CE) is the 'fifth Veda' of theatre — the text behind every classical form's grammar.

questions.question: Kathak's characteristic fast spins (chakkars) developed in the courts of:
questions.rationale: Kathak grew in the Mughal darbar — the reason it alone among the eight carries a courtly rather than temple lineage.

questions.question: Garba and Dandiya Raas are folk dances of:
questions.rationale: Both belong to Gujarat's Navratri nights — Dandiya's paired sticks distinguish it from Garba's clapped circular form.

questions.question: Which folk dance is a UNESCO-recognised intangible cultural heritage of Rajasthan?
questions.rationale: The Kalbelia — the snake-charmer community's sensuous dance — was inscribed by UNESCO in 2010; Chhau (eastern India) is the other dance on the list.

questions.question: The pacha (green) makeup of noble heroes is a signature of:
questions.rationale: Kathakali's colour code — pacha green for heroes, kathi knives for villains — turns the painted face into the drama's grammar.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam, the 'dance of the enchantress', comes from:
questions.rationale: Kerala's lasya-style women's dance joins Kathakali as the state's second classical form — the state pairing is the question's real test.
